text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko asked the major PZU insurance firm's president Jan Monkiewicz to lower its proposed new rates for obligatory motor liability premiums.

- U.S. company Ameritech sold its 24.5 percent stake in the Polish Centertel analogue mobile telephone firm to Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), Poland's state-owned telecom monopolist, and to France Telecom (FT). TPSA increased its stake to 66 percent and FT to 34 percent, the companies said.
- Japan's Isuzu diesel engine maker, co-owned by U.S. company General Motors (GM), will invest 380 million marks in Poland, Industry Minister Klemens Scierski said.

- In January 1996 Poland's transport ministry will call a tender to choose the privatisation advisor of LOT Polish Airlines, the transport ministry's aviation department director Ryszard Zaremba said.
- The EU and Japan will fund vocational training for 2,500 workers and help to create 1,000 new jobs in the Mielec region, southeastern Poland, the Mielec regional development agency (ARR) said.

- The Era GSM digital mobile phone network has cut its subscription price by 107 zlotys to 588.5 zlotys and its subscribers will soon be able to get connections in 50 cities, Era representative Robert Niczewski said.
- A third trawler ordered by a family group of Scottish fishermen was launched by Szczecin-based Parnica shipyard yesterday. It will enter operation in April next year.
- Sweden's Munksjo Forpackningar AB, which runs an envelope plant in Poland, will invest $12.5 million in construction of a cardboard packaging plant in Pruszkow, near Warsaw.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland's commercial banks' gross profit in the first nine months of 1996 was almost 200 percent higher than in the same period last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- The Penetrator securities house will produce a closed-end fund offer following the passage of the trust fund act in parliament, Pentrator's president Andrzej Madej said.

- Germany's investments in Poland this year were worth $750 million, while Polish investments in Germany reached $350 million. Registered trade between the two will exceed 1995 results by 12 percent, deputy foreign trade minister Jan Chaladaj said.

- The Lublin-based Lubelska Fabryka Maszyn Rolniczych (LFMR) farm machinery maker has received the International Standards Organisation (ISO)-9001 quality certificate from Germany's RW TUV auditing firm.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The listed Forte furniture maker's net profit in 1997 will be 26 million zlotys, the management's forecast said.
ZYCIE
- Customs duties on wheat, maize and other consumer grains' imports will be suspended till June 1997, the government said.
- Denmark's Christian Hansen biotechnology firm has invested around two $2 million in its Polish branch. The firm makes bacterial cultures for the dairy industry.
PARKIET

- The Warsaw-based Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych (BIG) is ready to take over a 31.4 percent stake in the Bank Gdanski (BG) bank, recently offered by the finance ministry, BIG bank's spokesman Wojciech Kaczorowski said.
- CS First Boston recommended selling the shares of the Bydgoszcz based BFK cable maker due to growing competition in the market, the bank's report dated November 18 said.
- The listed Pekpol meat processor and trader plans to acquire up to three new meat processing plants next year, Pekpol said.
- The Polish Life Improvement (PLI) wholesaler and retailer issued commercial papers worth five million zlotys.
